title: feat(whyk7): t(7,0,0)=13 via seed-exit to (0,-1,0) then support-drop
science: Structural explanation of the same-k death in #6786, and the clearest asymptotic statement in the slice: the lex-first walks show the axis arrival pays seed-exit 3 PLUS a final support-drop 3 on top of k-1 unit hops (t(7,0,0)=13 = 7+6), while the body-diagonal walk pays only the seed-exit and then 3k-1 unit hops with NO support drop (t(7,7,7)=23 = 21+2). So t_axis ~ k+6 and t_body ~ 3k+2, and the ratio test 3(k+6)^2 vs (3k+2)^2 tends to 3k^2 vs 9k^2 -- the reversal must fail for all large k, which is exactly what the k-sweeps observe.
verdict_pair: same-k reverse k=7 = NO (507<529), with the two lex-first walks exhibited
